title: A 3.0 envelope carrying a stray top-level 2.x imp[] is still validated as 3.0, with the mix flagged
specNotes: OpenRTB 3.0 §Object: OpenRTB defines the transport envelope as `{ver, domainspec, domainver, request|response}`; 2.x root fields such as `imp[]`/`seatbid[]` have no place inside or beside that envelope. A payload carrying a real 3.0 `openrtb.request` envelope AND a stray top-level `imp[]` mixes the two generations and is malformed with respect to both, not a legitimate hybrid.

The tool resolves this the same way it resolves the 2.x hybrid case (`mut-input-shape-hybrid-imp-and-seatbid`): the real 3.0 envelope wins (it is a fully-formed `openrtb.request`, unlike the empty-envelope fallback case documented in the core validation map), the payload is validated as 3.0, and `payload.ambiguous_envelope` names which layer won (`params.validated: '3.0'`) and says the other layer was ignored — rather than silently validating one layer with no acknowledgement of the mix.

This is a documented correct-behavior case, not a defect. The base pair bn-banner-30-adcom's own request already carries the informational `request.30.deep_validation_limited` finding independent of this mutation; `maxLevel: warning` tolerates it.
